strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing genuine challenges in multi-subject video generation with clear practical relevance
Comprehensive technical approach combining region-aware masking, subject disentanglement, and systematic data curation into an integrated framework

Extensive experimental validation with 120 reference-text pairs, multiple evaluation metrics (ID-Sim, Aesthetic, Motion, GmeScore, Subj-Sim, Bg-Sim), and consistent improvements over both open-source and proprietary baselines
Thorough ablation studies (Tables 3-4) demonstrating the contribution of each component and validating design choices
Excellent qualitative results across diverse scenarios (humans, animals, clothing, accessories, backgrounds, multi-subject scenes) with clear identity preservation
High-quality benchmark creation with careful curation and comprehensive evaluation infrastructure
User study validation providing human evaluation evidence for method effectiveness
Clear presentation with well-organized methodology, detailed appendices describing data pipeline stages, and good visual illustrations
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: region-aware masking and pixel-wise channel concatenation are incremental improvements over existing masking strategies; main contribution is careful engineering rather than fundamental innovation

Severe scope limitation: restricted to 5-second videos only (24-25 fps), cannot handle long-form video generation, significantly limiting practical applicability compared to recent video generation models

Complex data pipeline scalability concerns: 4-stage curation requiring SAM2, InsightFace, and multiple filtering steps lacks quantitative computational cost analysis; potential selection bias from aggressive filtering

Missing architectural analysis: no discussion of computational overhead from adding 2C channels via concatenation, no memory/latency comparison with baselines, limited justification for hyperparameter choices
Incomplete failure analysis: only 2 failure cases shown (Figure 14), lacks systematic characterization of failure modes and analysis of which subject combinations fail most frequently
Critical missing ablation: no systematic study of how number of reference images affects performance; current evaluation uses only 3 reference images, leaving key design parameter unexplored

Evaluation metric limitations: GmeScore relies on CLIP/BLIP with known issues for long text prompts; Subject Similarity requires ground-truth segmentation masks introducing potential bias; modest benchmark size (120 pairs)
Text encoding limitation: uses Qwen2.5-VL instead of MLLMs, limiting semantic understanding of complex descriptions; acknowledged as future work but represents current constraint

Reproducibility gaps: depends on multiple external tools with version dependencies (SAM2, InsightFace, Qwen2.5-VL); complex data pipeline difficult to reproduce exactly; no code/model release mentioned

strengths: Addresses a practically important and well-motivated problem of any-reference video generation with multiple diverse subjects, going beyond single-reference scenarios

Comprehensive experimental validation with multiple complementary metrics (ID-Sim, Aesthetic, Motion, GmeScore, Subj-Sim, Bg-Sim), evaluation on both single-ID and multi-subject settings, comparisons with 10+ baselines, and user study with 30 participants

Well-designed framework that coherently combines three complementary contributions: region-aware masking for appearance consistency, subject disentanglement for identity separation, and four-stage data pipeline for artifact mitigation
Consistent improvements across diverse evaluation metrics and settings, demonstrating robustness of the approach
Extensive ablation studies and supplementary materials including failure case analysis, additional qualitative results, and detailed evaluation metrics, supporting reproducibility
Clear mathematical formulations and detailed description of methods, hyperparameters, and experimental setup enabling reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited novelty of individual technical components; the approach primarily combines existing techniques (masking, text embedding injection, existing detection/segmentation models) rather than introducing fundamentally new concepts
Quantitative improvements are consistent but sometimes incremental (e.g., single-ID Total Score: 0.694 vs 0.687 for best baseline represents ~1% improvement)
Insufficient justification and analysis of key design decisions, such as why pixel-wise channel concatenation is superior to alternatives; limited ablation on component integration strategies
Restricted scope: limited to short videos (max 129 frames/5 seconds), cannot handle controllable long video generation, and restricted to text and image modalities without audio or 3D information

Complex four-stage data pipeline relying on multiple pre-trained models makes full reproduction challenging; unclear how much improvement comes from algorithmic contribution versus careful data curation
Lacks computational cost analysis, inference time comparisons, and detailed sensitivity analysis of the four-stage pipeline stages
Dense paper presentation with many interdependent components; some sections could be more concise and clearer in showing connections between components
